## PCA

```{r}
# Calculate principal components
pca_res <- prcomp(t(data_log), scale. = FALSE)

# Factoextra function to plot individuals from prcomp output
fviz_pca_ind(pca_res,
             geom = "point",
             col.ind = metadata$Virus,
             pointshape = metadata$Timepoint,
             addEllipses = FALSE,
             palette = "jco",
             pointsize = 2) +
  theme_minimal() +

```

## Viral trajectories

```{r}
# Extract coordinates and merge with metadata
pca_data <- as.data.frame(pca_res$x[, 1:2])
pca_data$Virus <- metadata$Virus
pca_data$Timepoint <- metadata$Timepoint

# Calculate centroids for each condition
centroids <- aggregate(cbind(PC1, PC2) ~ Virus + Timepoint, data = pca_data, FUN = mean)
centroids <- centroids[order(centroids$Timepoint), ] 

# Plot individuals with trajectory arrows
ggplot(pca_data, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = Virus)) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = Timepoint), size = 3, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_path(data = centroids, 
            aes(group = Virus), 
            arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.15, "inches"), type = "closed"),
            linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("H3N2"="#377EB8", "H7N7"="#FF7F00", 
                                "H7N9"="#984EA3", "mock"="#E41A1C", 
                                "VN1203"="#4DAF4A")) +
  labs(title = "Viral Transcriptomic Trajectories Over Time",
       x = "Dim 1", y = "Dim 2") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

# DEGs

## T-Test Function

```{r}
# Function to calculate Fold Change and P-value for a specific virus at 24h vs Mock 24h
run_deg_analysis <- function(data_matrix, target_virus) {
  
  # Identify column indices for the target virus and the mock control at 24h
  idx_virus <- grep(paste0("^", target_virus, "_24h"), colnames(data_matrix))
  idx_mock <- grep("^mock_24h", colnames(data_matrix))
  
  # Apply t-test row by row (gene by gene)
  results <- t(apply(data_matrix, 1, function(gene_expr) {
    expr_virus <- gene_expr[idx_virus]
    expr_mock <- gene_expr[idx_mock]
    
    # Calculate log2 Fold Change (mean of virus minus mean of mock)
    # Since data is already log2 transformed: log2(A) - log2(B) = log2(A/B)
    logFC <- mean(expr_virus) - mean(expr_mock)
    
    # Run t-test (suppress errors if variance is 0)
    p_val <- tryCatch(
      t.test(expr_virus, expr_mock, var.equal = TRUE)$p.value,
      error = function(e) NA
    )
    
    return(c(logFC = logFC, pvalue = p_val))
  }))
  
  # Convert to dataframe
  res_df <- as.data.frame(results)
  res_df$Gene <- rownames(res_df)
  
  # Apply Multiple Testing Correction (Benjamini-Hochberg FDR)
  res_df$padj <- p.adjust(res_df$pvalue, method = "BH")
  
  return(res_df)
}
```

## Run T-Tests for each virus

```{r}
# Run the analysis for each virus vs Mock at 24h
deg_H7N9 <- run_deg_analysis(data_log, "H7N9")
deg_H3N2 <- run_deg_analysis(data_log, "H3N2")
deg_H7N7 <- run_deg_analysis(data_log, "H7N7")
deg_VN1203 <- run_deg_analysis(data_log, "VN1203")

# Check the top most significant genes for H7N9
head(deg_H7N9[order(deg_H7N9$padj), ])
```

## Significant dysregulated genes

```{r}
# Count how many DEGs each virus triggered at 24h, up or downregulated by more than double or half
sig_threshold <- function(df) {
  sum(df$padj < 0.05 & abs(df$logFC) > 1, na.rm = TRUE)
}

cat("Significant DEGs at 24h:\n",
    "H7N9: ", sig_threshold(deg_H7N9), "\n",
    "H3N2: ", sig_threshold(deg_H3N2), "\n",
    "H7N7: ", sig_threshold(deg_H7N7), "\n",
    "VN1203: ", sig_threshold(deg_VN1203), "\n")
```

## Venn Diagrams for DEGs

```{r}
# Extract significant upregulated and downregulated genes
get_up_genes <- function(df) df[which(df$padj < 0.05 & df$logFC > 1), "Gene"]
get_down_genes <- function(df) df[which(df$padj < 0.05 & df$logFC < -1), "Gene"]

list_UP <- list(
  H3N2   = get_up_genes(deg_H3N2),
  H7N7   = get_up_genes(deg_H7N7),
  H7N9   = get_up_genes(deg_H7N9),
  VN1203 = get_up_genes(deg_VN1203)
)

list_DOWN <- list(
  H3N2   = get_down_genes(deg_H3N2),
  H7N7   = get_down_genes(deg_H7N7),
  H7N9   = get_down_genes(deg_H7N9),
  VN1203 = get_down_genes(deg_VN1203)
)

# Plot Upregulated DEGs intersection
plot_UP <- ggVennDiagram(list_UP, label_alpha = 0, set_size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F4FAFE", high = "#E41A1C") +
  labs(title = "Upregulated Genes at 24h", subtitle = "padj < 0.05, log2FC > 1") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Plot Downregulated DEGs intersection
plot_DOWN <- ggVennDiagram(list_DOWN, label_alpha = 0, set_size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F4FAFE", high = "#377EB8") +
  labs(title = "Downregulated Genes at 24h", subtitle = "padj < 0.05, log2FC < -1") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

plot_UP
plot_DOWN
```

```{r}
# Isolate H7N9 exclusive genes for downstream functional enrichment
unique_up_H7N9 <- setdiff(list_UP$H7N9, c(list_UP$H3N2, list_UP$H7N7, list_UP$VN1203))
unique_down_H7N9 <- setdiff(list_DOWN$H7N9, c(list_DOWN$H3N2, list_DOWN$H7N7, list_DOWN$VN1203))
```

## Heatmap targeted on H7N9 dysregulated genes

```{r}
# 1. Combine the unique up and down genes into one list
h7n9_exclusive_genes <- c(unique_up_H7N9, unique_down_H7N9)

# 2. Subset the main log2 normalized matrix to keep only these genes
# We isolate only the 24h samples to keep the visual clean and focused
idx_24h <- grep("_24h", colnames(data_log))
matrix_24h <- data_log[h7n9_exclusive_genes, idx_24h]

# 3. Scale the data by row (gene) to highlight relative differences across viruses
# This centers each gene around 0, making patterns instantly visible
matrix_scaled <- t(scale(t(matrix_24h)))

# 4. Create annotation dataframe for the top of the heatmap
annotation_col <- data.frame(
  Virus = sapply(strsplit(colnames(matrix_24h), "_"), `[`, 1)
)
rownames(annotation_col) <- colnames(matrix_24h)

# Define matching colors for the annotation
ann_colors <- list(
  Virus = c(H3N2 = "#377EB8", H7N7 = "#FF7F00", 
            H7N9 = "#984EA3", mock = "#E41A1C", VN1203 = "#4DAF4A")
)

# 5. Generate the heatmap
pheatmap(matrix_scaled, 
         cluster_cols = TRUE,    # Cluster samples based on expression similarity
         cluster_rows = FALSE,    # Cluster genes with similar patterns
         show_rownames = FALSE,  # Hide 2,000+ gene names to keep it readable
         annotation_col = annotation_col,
         annotation_colors = ann_colors,
         color = colorRampPalette(c("navy", "white", "firebrick3"))(50),
         main = "Expression Profile of H7N9-Exclusive DEGs at 24h",
         fontsize_col = 8)
```

### ReactomePA

```{r}
# 1. Convert Gene Symbols to Entrez IDs (Required by most pathway databases)
genes_up_entrez <- bitr(unique_up_H7N9, 
                        fromType = "SYMBOL", 
                        toType = "ENTREZID", 
                        OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db)

genes_down_entrez <- bitr(unique_down_H7N9, 
                          fromType = "SYMBOL", 
                          toType = "ENTREZID", 
                          OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db)

# 2. Run Reactome Enrichment Analysis (Relaxing the UP cutoff to see trends)
reactome_up <- enrichPathway(gene = genes_up_entrez$ENTREZID, 
                             organism = "human", 
                             pvalueCutoff = 0.2,   # Relaxed threshold to force output
                             readable = TRUE)

reactome_down <- enrichPathway(gene = genes_down_entrez$ENTREZID, 
                               organism = "human", 
                               pvalueCutoff = 0.05, 
                               readable = TRUE)

# 3. Visualize Top Pathways (Adding label_format to wrap long text)
dotplot(reactome_up, showCategory = 15, 
        title = "Reactome: Upregulated in H7N9 (Exclusive)", 
        label_format = 40)

dotplot(reactome_down, showCategory = 15, 
        title = "Reactome: Downregulated in H7N9 (Exclusive)", 
        label_format = 50) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7, lineheight = 0.8))
```

### EnrichR (GO, KEGG)

```{r}
# 1. Define the reference databases to capture a multi-dimensional biological profile:
# - GO Biological Process (BP): Identifies the overarching systemic responses (e.g., immune evasion, cell death).
# - GO Molecular Function (MF): Highlights the specific biochemical activities of the dysregulated proteins.
# - GO Cellular Component (CC): Maps subcellular localization to show where the virus hijacks host machinery.
# - KEGG: Maps the gene lists to well-established signaling and metabolic pathways.
dbs <- c("GO_Biological_Process_2023", 
         "GO_Molecular_Function_2023", 
         "GO_Cellular_Component_2023", 
         "KEGG_2021_Human")

# 2. Query the EnrichR API using the isolated H7N9-exclusive gene symbols.
# This statistically evaluates which biological concepts are significantly 
# over-represented in our specific viral signature compared to random chance.
enrich_up <- enrichr(unique_up_H7N9, dbs)
enrich_down <- enrichr(unique_down_H7N9, dbs)

# 3. Visualize Cellular Component (CC) for Downregulated genes.
# Identifying suppressed structural components often reveals which host barriers 
# or antigen presentation machinery the virus actively dismantles (e.g., cell surface).
plotEnrich(enrich_down[["GO_Cellular_Component_2023"]], 
           showTerms = 15, 
           numChar = 50, 
           y = "Count", 
           orderBy = "P.value") +
  ggtitle("GO Cellular Component: Downregulated uniquely in H7N9") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10))

# 4. Visualize Biological Process (BP) for Downregulated genes.
# This complements the CC spatial data by showing exactly which functional 
# defense programs the virus is shutting down at those subcellular locations.
plotEnrich(enrich_down[["GO_Biological_Process_2023"]], 
           showTerms = 15, 
           numChar = 50, 
           y = "Count", 
           orderBy = "P.value") +
  ggtitle("GO Biological Process: Downregulated uniquely in H7N9") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10))
```

# Volcano plots

```{r}
# Function to generate a standardized Volcano Plot
plot_volcano <- function(deg_df, virus_name) {
  
  # 1. Categorize genes based on our exact thresholds
  deg_df$Regulation <- "Not Significant"
  deg_df$Regulation[deg_df$logFC > 1 & deg_df$padj < 0.05] <- "Upregulated"
  deg_df$Regulation[deg_df$logFC < -1 & deg_df$padj < 0.05] <- "Downregulated"
  
  # Enforce factor levels for consistent coloring
  deg_df$Regulation <- factor(deg_df$Regulation, 
                              levels = c("Downregulated", "Not Significant", "Upregulated"))
  
  # 2. Extract the top 15 most significant genes for labeling
  top_genes <- head(deg_df[order(deg_df$padj), ], 15)
  
  # 3. Build the plot mapping magnitude (logFC) against significance (-log10 padj)
  ggplot(deg_df, aes(x = logFC, y = -log10(padj), color = Regulation)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.2) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Downregulated" = "#377EB8", 
                                  "Not Significant" = "grey80", 
                                  "Upregulated" = "#E41A1C")) +
    # Add threshold lines
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed", color = "black", alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "black", alpha = 0.5) +
    # Add non-overlapping labels for top genes
    geom_text_repel(data = top_genes, aes(label = Gene), 
                    size = 3, color = "black", max.overlaps = 20) +
    labs(title = paste(virus_name, "Transcriptomic Response"),
         subtitle = "24h post-infection vs Mock control",
         x = "Magnitude of Change (Log2 Fold Change)",
         y = "Statistical Significance (-Log10 Adjusted P-value)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
}

# Generate and display the Volcano plot for H7N9
volcano_H7N9 <- plot_volcano(deg_H7N9, "H7N9")
volcano_H7N9

# Volcano plots for other viruses
plot_volcano(deg_H3N2, "H3N2")
plot_volcano(deg_H7N7, "H7N7")
plot_volcano(deg_VN1203, "VN1203")
```
